extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders preparing public comments on proposed FLSA rules (employers, employees, industry groups, advocacy organizations, lawyers, economists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting effective public comments on Department of Labor (Wage and Hour Division) proposed Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) rules, including procedural requirements, substantive evidence to provide, and common topics to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of submission / identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted, identified by Regulatory Information Number (RIN), through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via the Federal eRulemaking Portal and include the RIN so the comment is associated with the correct rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before the deadline specified in the Federal Register notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent FLSA rules have had ~60-day comment periods; ensure submission is before the Federal Register deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific FLSA statutory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific FLSA sections (29 USC §§ 201-219).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground legal arguments in precise statutory citations to show how the rule relates to or interprets statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference implementing regulations (29 CFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference 29 CFR provisions being amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and discuss the specific regulatory provisions that the proposed rule would change or interpret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with DOL Field Operations Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with relevant DOL Field Operations Handbook sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Handbook to show how enforcement guidance and operational practices intersect with the proposed regulatory change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Wage and Hour Opinion Letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Wage and Hour Opinion Letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Opinion Letters as administrative interpretations and supportive precedent for positions taken in the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference federal court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference federal court FLSA decisions (Encino Motorcars, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring in controlling or persuasive case law to support legal arguments about statutory interpretation, exemptions, or standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide industry-specific data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide industry-specific data on wages, hours, classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply empirical evidence tied to the affected industries (e.g., restaurants, retail, healthcare, construction) to show real-world impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address impact on small employers (RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address impact on small employers (Regulatory Flexibility Act considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed rule affects small entities and include data or analysis that would inform RFA compliance and potential exemptions or mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide economic impact estimates with verifiable assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite economic impact estimates with verifiable assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include transparent, reproducible estimates and clearly state assumptions, data sources, and methods so the agency can evaluate and, if necessary, quantify impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with state parallel wage-hour laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with state wage-hour law parallel provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how federal proposals interact with state laws, including conflicts, complementarities, and administrative burdens for multi-jurisdictional employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address worker misclassification concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Address worker misclassification concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence and argumentation about how the rule would affect classification of employees vs. independent contractors and implications for enforcement and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tax form trends data (1099/W-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite IRS Form 1099 and W-2 data trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference tax-reporting trends to support claims about workforce composition, misclassification, and economic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address gig economy / platform worker issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Address gig economy / platform worker considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed rule would affect platform-based work, including classification, hours, pay practices, and enforcement challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overtime exempt/non-exempt salary thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss overtime exempt/non-exempt salary thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data and policy arguments about appropriate salary tests, indexing, regional adjustments, and impacts on workers and employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent contractor vs. employee classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Address independent contractor versus employee classification standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze tests or standards proposed, provide industry examples, and present evidence on how different rules would change classification outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint employer standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Address joint employer standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss factors that determine joint employer status, implications for liability and compliance, and provide factual scenarios or data illustrating impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tip pooling and tip credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Address tip pooling and tip credit rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how proposed changes affect tipped workers, employer crediting, distribution of tips, and compliance burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companionship services exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the companionship services exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual and legal analysis regarding whether and how the exemption should apply, with examples from the caregiving/homecare sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer professional exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the computer professional exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the criteria for the exemption, typical job duties, salary levels, and industry practice; include examples and data where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: White collar exemptions (executive, administrative, professional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address white collar exemptions (executive, administrative, professional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze duties tests, salary thresholds, bonuses, and other factors that determine exemption status; provide occupational data and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside sales exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the outside sales exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the exemption applies in modern sales roles, remote work contexts, and industry-specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonus and incentive payment treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Address treatment of bonus and incentive payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how non-salary payments should be counted toward salary tests or overtime calculations, and provide examples and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hours worked / portal-to-portal issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Address hours worked and portal-to-portal issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss what time counts as compensable work (e.g., travel, pre-shift activities) and provide factual scenarios or time-study data to support positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of detail / length of substantive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective DOL comments are typically detailed (10-30 pages for substantive rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For substantive rulemakings, provide comprehensive analysis, citations, data, and appendices as needed; short or vague comments are less persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support comments with economic literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Heavily cited to economic literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground empirical claims and projected impacts in peer-reviewed or reputable economic studies, and cite literature to bolster credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include compliance cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Include compliance cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative estimates of compliance costs with methods and assumptions documented so the agency can assess the economic impact analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address impacts on specific industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Address impact on specific industries (restaurants, retail, healthcare, construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor analysis to industry-specific business models, margins, labor practices, and operational realities to show differentiated effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multiple perspectives (employer and employee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with both employer and employee perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and analyze effects on workers and employers to present a balanced, robust comment that anticipates counterarguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss transition timelines and good-faith compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Address transition timelines and good-faith compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose realistic implementation timelines, training or notice periods, and describe how good-faith efforts should be treated in enforcement.
